commands.ping: answers pong; ping [-c n] <host>: ICMP echo over Ethernet like Linux's ping (names via DNS)
commands.ifconfig: the Ethernet port (a USB adapter with CDC ECM, an RTL8153's): MAC, address from DHCP, router
commands.dhcp: ask the DHCP server for an address again
commands.screen: draw on the test screen's picture (and show it): demo|bars|clear|text|rect|on|off
commands.testscreen: the demo's test screen on the TV (its boxes, the colour bars); a key on the USB keyboard or 'console' brings the console back
commands.console: the console on the TV: everything the UART shows, scrolling, PgUp/PgDn for earlier lines (the view after start)
commands.panel: front panel digits, brightness (boards with the TM1650)
commands.keys: front panel key state; without a TM1650 (Comsat TE 1050 HD) its two buttons on GPIO 31 / 9
commands.usb: USB port state, the descriptors of its device and, through a hub, of every device behind it; reset, init, kbd [report|interrupt|raw on|off] (a USB keyboard types into the command line, read from its interrupt endpoint), mouse (a USB mouse moves a pointer on the TV and paints with its left button), reg <offset> [byte], ctl <type> <request> <value> <index> <length> [device] (a control request)
commands.lsusb: the USB devices, one line each (with the hub and port of those behind a hub)
commands.disks: USB disks (sticks, card readers): their size, partitions and file systems
commands.ls: [n:][path]: a directory on a USB disk's FAT12 / FAT16 / FAT32 volume (n: the disk's device number as lsusb lists it; a path without '/' starts in the current directory)
commands.cd: [n:][path]: the current directory, shown in the prompt ('..' one up; alone: none)
commands.cat: [n:]path: a text file on a USB disk (Ctrl-C stops it)
commands.mkdir: <path>: make a directory (writes the disk; long names too)
commands.rmdir: <path>: remove an empty directory (writes the disk)
commands.touch: <path>: make an empty file (writes the disk)
commands.cp: <from> <to>: copy a file (to a directory: into it; onto another disk too)
commands.mv: <from> <to>: rename a file or directory, or move it into another directory of the same volume
commands.> / >>: after any command: what it prints goes into a file ('ls > 4:/list.txt'; >> adds to its end); "..." or '...' keep spaces in a word
commands.sector: [n:]<number>: one sector of a USB disk in hex
commands.tty: the USB serial ports: a GSM / LTE module's AT and diagnostic ports (SIMCom, Quectel, Huawei, ZTE ...), CDC ACM devices
commands.cu: [n]: the terminal joined to serial port ttyUSB<n> (without n: the module's AT port): what you type goes to it, what it sends is shown; "~." at a line's start or Ctrl-] ends
commands.at: [command]: one AT command to the module's AT port and its answer up to OK / ERROR, and what follows at once (AT+HTTPREAD's page); lines the module sent before (+HTTPACTION, RING) first ('at +csq', 'at i'; a line typed as AT... goes there too; > file works)
commands.watchdog: the chip's watchdog, running from the start: a demo stopped for 8 s restarts the box; test (stop feeding it), off, on
commands.history: the commands typed before (Up/Down recall them)
commands.video: the original firmware's display and HDMI set-up, per board and chip revision (init [opticum|comsat] [rev0|rev1]); the demo runs this board's at start, before USB
commands.bootloader: restart into the original bootloader; hold 'c' (or run the updater) to stay in it
commands.ccc: three 'c' on an empty line: restart for the UART updater's boot capture
commands./: every command may also be written with '/' in front (/restart)
